txt: A look of consternation crosses the man's face. He looks at you, then at his bottle, then back at you...
After what feels like ages, you hear the fence creaking as if under a large weight. Look at him. Just look at him.
Before you know it the man has put down the bottle, stood up, and left. Minutes pass; the clouds change shape up in the sky...
He breathes in deeply, preparing his recitation...
He clears his throat: "Summer of '44. Seventeen-year-old Gertrude Het is walking home from a late shift at the harbour. It's almost midnight. She stops for a cigarette near the canal..."
He cracks open a bottle and sucks the bitter foam welling at the top. "Do you want anything else or can I concentrate on my drinking?"
He freezes in his seat, motionless except his pupils, which quickly flick from side to side.
He raises his palm as if to shun you back to wherever you came from. "No-no-no, contrary to popular belief, I enjoy being alive."
He scans the document and lets out a long, low whistle. "Things have really turned around for you, haven't they? You've got *big money* problems now." He looks back at you, eyes gleaming.
He sighs. "It isn't that easy... But I'm working on it. I really am. I even signed up for this evening group in Jamrock."
He takes a swig, wipes his mouth, then continues. "That is, if he even existed. Who knows? It's an urban legend, after all..."
He taps against his head. "Askin' is how you get ahead."
He turns his swollen face against the snow, droplets of beer freezing in his beard.
He turns his swollen face against the wind, freezing rain battering his cheeks.
He turns his swollen nose to face the moon, cheeks ruddy from the biting wind.
He turns his swollen nose to face the sun, cheeks ruddy from the biting wind.
It's Idiot Doom Spiral -- he's *back*. Like a beast made of jaundice and fetid polypropylene, he returns locked in stiff combat and with a most fearsome foe...
The man falls ominously silent for a moment. "Her body is never recovered." He looks you straight in the eye.
The man in the stinking tracksuit nods solemnly. "Having a well-deserved break from your adventures. It's what we all need sometimes."
"'Awful' is very strong, Tequila. You're gonna have to explain how I missed the mark by *so much* if that's the case. What don't you like about it?"
"'FALN'? That's medium-concept stuff. Not my style at all... I can't believe I'm saying this, but maybe you should lay off the booze -- It's fucking with your head."
"'No thanks to the squares at the precinct', as you put it."
"'Sinus salt,' 'the white knight'...."
"'THE TIME HATH COME.'"
"*Domwtclall Abheqoeel*?" His friend grabs the document and admires it. "Great job, Abbs. Nailed it." He hands it back to you.
"*Millions* of reál generated for clients. I've made my name in this world."
"*Other* things? We're talking about your big moment here, your time to shine, your ascension into a household name."
"*Relax*. I see you both running around like maniacs, just back and forth, back and forth. Gotta live a little, enjoy the day."
"*Relax*. I see you both running around like maniacs, just back and forth, back and forth. Gotta live a little, enjoy the sun."
"*Relax*. I see you running around like a maniac, just back and forth, back and forth. Gotta live a little, enjoy the day."
"*Relax*. I see you running around like a maniac, just back and forth, back and forth. Gotta live a little, enjoy the sun."
"*The Cocaine Skull*!"
"*Wet*, okay? It was raining really hard." There's a trace of derision in his voice.
"... with no head on his shoulders! Wearing a FALN tracksuit. Searching for the legendary FALN cap that went missing -- when he lost his head."
"A headless man, wearing a FALN tracksuit, riding a horse. That's right. It's the *Headless FALN Rider*. "
"Acid gnomes? Sounds like a stupid, low-concept band name."
"After which your reality contracted -- you jammed the pedal, ploughed right off the jetty and through the ice."
"Ah, Tequila, I *knew* you'd come through. That's fucking great, man!"
"Ah, shit..."
"Aha!" He takes a sip from his beer. "Do you want to know how Tequila Sunset came to be?"
"All kinds. I've seen archaeologists, gangsters, even a bunch of ad agency types. I'm telling you, Tequila -- this thing's got a *pull* on certain kinds of people."
"Alright!" He grabs the pen and paper and carefully, scribbles on the dotted line -- next to Lilienne's signature -- 'Idiot Doom Spiral'.
"Alright!" He grabs the pen and paper from your hands and, very carefully, scribbles on the dotted line, next to 'Lilienne Carter': 'Idiot Doom Spiral'.
"Alright, I understand. We'll do this some other time, when you can focus on yourself and not this *inconvenience*."
"And I didn't even lose anything!" He stares into empty space, eyes like discarded bottle caps. "Okay, guess I'm back to where I was before. Square one. It's not like I haven't been here before."

"And forget about contractors and the like. This job I'm handling *personally*, concept and execution," he continues. "Any unexpected expenses we'll take care of later. Can't let price compromise the work. Easy."

"And second, outfitting an expedition like that is expensive. It'd have to be a *big production* to do the Cocaine Skull justice. You need new gear, people who know what they're doing, all kinds of provisions..."

"And that's only the start. Wait until the strike's over and the workers can finally deliver the product. I *guarantee* the papers will pick it up. You'll be the talk of the town -- -- investing into the community, creating value, giving back..."
"And this is Abs." He points to the man in the pipe. "So yeah, that's basically us. We drink together."
"And yeah, you're already acquainted with Abs." He points to the man in the pipe. "So yeah, that's basically us. We drink together."
"Anything else this merry band of adventurers can do for you, or do you need to go and mail that serious looking document of yours?" His face lightens up. "I think I saw a mailbox near the plaza."
"Anything else this merry band of adventurers can do for you, or do you need to go and mail that serious looking document of yours?" His face lightens up. "There's a mailbox on the plaza."
"Anything else you want?" He takes an enormous swig from the bottle, swaying back and forth.
"Anything else?" He throws one leg over another, smug and content.

"Anyway, long story short, life spiralled out of control. I haven't gotten into my apartment for years, and my girlfriend left me because she didn't want to date a homeless man. The company, well, you see where I'm going with this..."

"Anyway, sometime later he started his own personal studio here in Martinaise, and that's when he started working on some *really* wild stuff. I'm talking some glass-smooth, forward looking design language, the kind of thing that would totally overthrow the old regime, design-wise."
"Anyway, that's not the point. The point is that mixing art and sex can make you fucking *rich*.
"Anyway, that's the story of the *Headless FALN Rider*. Pretty crazy, huh?"
"Anyway, there was a brief silence -- a *gasp* of silence, if you will -- followed by a real commotion. We heard the carriage careening towards the coast at top speed."
"Anyway, to each his own. You want to hear any other stories?"

"Apparently the idea was *too* high-concept even for this genius. He dropped dead right at his desk before he could finish. His last words are recorded to have been: "It's as white as a blizzard... *of cocaine!*"

"At the Boom Boom Room I directed a team of *talent architects*. People so high concept their names were nothing but a single letter. We had *manic* ideas, fuelled by copious amounts of coffee-flavoured whey powder. We did stuff no one had ever seen before -- or *since*!"
"Beside your gun and your badge? You said something about your hope, or heart, or something. To be honest the details are a little hazy..."
"Bet you're glad you hired me as your Personal Brand Strategist now? So, what's next, boss?"
"Booze. Did you already forget our party?" He taps his finger to his temple. "The thing I relayed to you earlier?"
"But I've got something the others don't. I'm on *your* level. And as I already understand *your* needs I can marry my high-concept ideas with your brand easily. I'll help you make your mark."
"But Tequila..." He hangs his head in despair. "For what? I really tried to make it work this time -- for you, for me, for the triumph of *high-concept* ideas..."
"But are you *really* cornering the market is the question?"
"But if there's anything else your old friend can do for you, let me know." He takes a mouthful of beer, swishing it around in his mouth like some kind of sommelier.
"But now dreams are worn thin, much like my tracksuit," he says thoughtfully, brushing dust off his shit-stained pants.
"But that charm wears off pretty quickly. Before you know it, you're wearing a shit-stained tracksuit and spending your days picking tare."
"But the story doesn't end there. Supposedly, when they performed the autopsy, the coroner discovered nearly a *quarter kilo of coke* jammed into his nasal cavity."
"But then, something turned. You see, it's widely known that *nose candy* and pioneer graphic design work go hand-in-hand..."
"But there is no lightning. Only a heavy downpour and the silhouette of the *Headless FALN Rider* looming on the horizon!"
"But what matters is that it's true to my subjective experience. Anyway, that was all the story one bottle gets you." He looks at it. "Almost empty this one..."
"But when I reached my office I remembered that I'd asked one of my producers to change the locks that day -- and since I hired only the best, he'd already done it, and I couldn't get in..."
"By now I'd say I know about as much about it as anyone on the coast."
"Can't really remember seeing any women after losing my keys."
"Classy." He snatches the bottle and pushes the cork in through the bottleneck.
"Coincidentally, at that exact moment, a horse happened to pass under him and his beheaded corpse mounted it, where it remains to this day... But then, no one really knows."
"Cotton mouth is keeping my tongue imprisoned." He shrugs his shoulders dramatically.
"Damn right it doesn't. So why don't you just shut up and leave it to the *master*?"

"Didn't I already say, I don't wanna be the one who breaks it to you? You have to get acquainted with *the event* first! It'd be irresponsible..." The man shakes his head. His gray eyes look into yours.
"Didn't I tell you?" He turns to his drinking buddy. "I told him, didn't I? Several times. This is what I *do*."
"Different *how*? Business is business. Doesn't matter if it's small or large, I handle it for you now -- that's what you hired me to do."
"Do you always try to pick the lamest option possible? Come on, Tequila!"
"Do you have anything to fortify ol' Doom Spiral? Tell me you got some story juice."
"Do you want anything else? If not, I've got some serious drinking to do..."
"Don't be shy, Tequila. Of course I'll do it." He ploughs a thumb into his chest. "I'm your man."
"Don't know if I've mentioned it, but I used to be a businessman and *as* a businessman I am going to keep the pen for my trouble." He nods confidently.
"Don't listen to him or his grandma. He's just making things up."
"Don't mind ol' Rosemary here, he's a buffoon." The tracksuited man waves his hand at you. "Let's have a word after your high-concept transactions, I'll give you the lowdown."
"Don't sit on it. Keep the hard stuff moving."
"Don't spend a single brain cell worrying about it, just leave it all to me... the final outcome will be *spectacular*. Just takes a little time..."

"Drinking is the fuel to my fire. Moistens me up to ensure the high concepts have a smooth landing." He tries taking another sip from the bottle, but misses and pours some of its contents inside his collar.
"Either bring it back the way it was before, or find a dumpster to burn it in." He hands it to you.

"Either way, it was a late Saturday night, when we, the Union of Moribund Alcoholics, got our drink on. Nothing remarkable about this, we get our drink on 24/7. Makes everything warm and glowy, I trust you know the feeling."
"Exactly! I just know I wouldn't be able to deliver the hot shit you're after without it." He has a quick swig from his bottle.
"Exactly! Just give me a minute or two..."
"Exactly! We're partners, you and I -- partners in drinking, partners in business..." He chugs in celebration.
"Excellent." He rubs his hands together. "When can you get started? The sooner I get that jacket back, the sooner I can get my life back together."
"Excuse me, are you telling the story, now? No? You're not? Well then..." He scoffs.
"Fine. You know what? Fuck it. You'll be back, Tequila. You wanna go -- you go. This isn't the end. I'm taking you all the way to the top."
"For one, the way is blocked... by that big lorry that says 'Delta Logistics Company' on the side. You'd *definitely* have to search the area behind that lorry too. Yet it is impassable."
"Fuck yeah they will. Tequila Sunset is on the timeline. They'll be talking about you for years. The one and only."
"Fuck, Rosemary, they were dating -- no one said they were feminists. Everyone always misremembering this stuff..."
"Fuck..." He lets his head drop between his arms. "Well, that's that. At least I tried." A long and heavy breath out, a few sloppy sucks on his bottle.
"Fucking hell, Tequila. Don't do that to me. I appreciate being kept on my toes, but *man*!" He shakes his head to straighten himself out.
"Gave herself facial deconstruction surgery. Real grisly stuff."
"Gertrude Het may have been the first to witness the *Headless FALN Rider*, but she wasn't the last, oh no..."
"Giants? That the best you got? Give me a break, Tequila."
"Gimme more, gimme more. What do you like most about it?" He's giddy -- both from the drink and the anticipation.
"Give me half an hour, my friend. In fact," he raises his grubby finger again, "I demand you to *sit down here* and *not move* until I'm back. Open a beer, chat with your old pals..."
"Glad to have been of assistance!" He gives you a thumbs up, and the envelope also. "After all this time, I feel like I've made a difference..."
"Glad to have been of assistance!" He gives you a thumbs up. "After all this time, I feel like I've made a difference..."
"Go on then, what exactly isn't doing it for you?" He wraps both hands around his bottle and leans forward, ready to listen.
"God bless them, though. I'd be alone without them. Anyway, that was all the story one bottle gets you." He turns his eyes to the bottle. "Almost empty this one..."
"Good fucking question, Tequila! If I knew the answer, you think I'd be hanging out on a beach in this formerly premium but now extremely dirty two-piece Lickra(TM) tracksuit?"

"Good one, boss." He laughs weakly but stops when he realises you're being serious. "What -- really? That's it? You can't cut it short *now*. We're just getting started. At least give me an explanation."
"Good thing, because I don't think you can find it right now anyway."
"Good to see you! How's business? How's the whole *reality situation* treating you?"
"Gotta ride this one out."
"Great!" He scans your face for any telltale signs of a verdict. "Great."
"HEY ABS! ABS!" He grabs his passed-out friend by the shoulder and shakes him a bit.
"Here he is! The man, the reality, the *financial czar*." He presents you to the group as if on a stage. "You seen it yet?"
"Here's the kicker -- this designer, this *lead designer* of a world famous design studio -- was *born* in Martinaise. A local boy. Martin Martinaise."
"Hey Abs!" He shouts to the mumbling drunkard next to him. "HEY ABS!"
"Hey Abs!" He shouts to the non-responsive drunk still dribbling drool from the side of his mouth.
"Hey man, I'm not judging." He waves the bottle towards you. "This life's a valley of woes. Some of the highest-concept people in history have killed themselves -- *and* been drunks."
"Hey! Goddamn *Abigail* is here, wake up! WAKE UP!" His efforts get no response.
"Hey, HEY. Fuck you, Tequila," he says, his voice level.
"Hey, Tequila! Welcome to reality. How's it treating you?" A thirty-something Lickra(TM)-clad man takes a sip from his beer.
"Hey, Tequila!" A thirty-something man clad in a two-piece Lickra(TM) tracksuit puts down his pilsner and extends his hand in greeting.

"Hey, Tequila, pay attention! The story goes that one day he was balls-deep in work on what he thought would be his *pièce de résistance*: An advert so *minimal* it contained neither text nor images. Just... pure white..."
"Hey, guys -- I'm a hero!" He hands you the envelope, and waves his hand erratically at his companions.
"Hey, guys -- we're heroes!" He waves his hand erratically to the other guys.
"Hey, let's not jump ahead of ourselves, this is *your* story. Stop interrupting." He takes another sip -- then continues.
"High-concept business venture." The man nods. "Solid vision, stellar execution."
"Hmmm." The man examines the jacket for a moment, a look of consternation on his brow...
"Holy shit! Tequila, how did you? Never mind -- I don't care, just let me see the jacket."
"Hours. It was an all-night drink-a-thon. Then at some point -- I think it was Sunday morning -- you got belligerent and wanted to talk about *Revacholian women*."
"How they're beautiful and also whores and so on. How one of them fucked you real bad. After a short while you crossed the event horizon, looked sullen, got up, and left without saying anything."
"I *guarantee* the papers will pick it up once it's all finished, with photos and everything. You'll be the talk of the town -- investing into the community, creating value, giving back..."
"I *guarantee* the papers will pick it up, with photos and everything. You'll be the talk of the town -- investing into the community, creating value, giving back..."
"I *know*..." He takes a long, wistful sip of his pilsner. "It was fucking awesome. And now it's all gone."
"I actually do have one... the strangest of them all. But I'll need to *fortify* myself before I can tell that one..."
"I believe you mentioned something about the ground cracking open to swallow cities and dreams alike. Yeah... I remember that *simile* or whatever the fuck they are."
"I can already see it -- Tequila Sunset -- spelled out in cathode rays. Luminous against the evening sky. There won't be a single kid in this town who doesn't know who you are."
"I can't say it increased my faith in the RCM. No offence, gentlemen." He shakes his head.
"I convinced my partners to reinvest some of our profits in an even-more high-concept 'cultural incubator' called 'Thin Air'. The artists were happy, the clients were happy."
"I developed the paradigm, worked within the paradigm. But the burden of leadership weighed heavily on me, so I went jogging every so often to keep myself sane."
"I didn't agree with you, by the way. The spectral hand of the market makes sure everyone gets exactly what they deserve." He takes a long sip of beer.
"I didn't say renovating, I said *re-conceptualization*. It's medium-concept shit is what it is," he says, spitting out each word.
"I do -- but as you can see my fuel tank is running quite low, if you catch my drift..." He spins the bottle in his hand. Not a single drop of liquid remains.
"I don't *want* it, man." His eyes light up. "I *need* it. Can't tell stories without it -- dry stories are boring, you see."
"I don't remember you being such a dick before, Tequila..." He takes a slow, despondent sip from his bottle, then looks out across the bay toward the glittering lights of La Delta at night.
"I don't remember you being such a dick before, Tequila..." He takes a slow, despondent sip from his bottle, then looks out across the bay toward the skyscrapers of La Delta.
"I don't think *I* can do it. Sorry." He stares at the bottle in his hand, then lets out a deep sigh...

"I don't think you're ready for that *grade* of reality yet. It'd be ill-advised for me to tell you. You gotta go do the *intro* yourself -- come back when you've been to the motor carriage, Tequila." He sips his beer.
"I have to admit, that's pretty high-concept. Still not as awesome as a headless rider in a FALN tracksuit, though."
"I knew it! That's what you get when you hire me -- customer satisfaction guaranteed. Woo!"
"I know what you mean. Sitting around with these bums you really get to know the nitty-gritty of *reality*. And it isn't good." He looks at his buddies with mock appreciation.

"I know, I know. Ran into some problems there -- material shortages and the like -- but don't worry, genius *thrives* under constraints!" He points at himself, proud and happy. "That's why you pay for the best..."
"I know, Tequila, I know..." He takes a swig, considers pouring some out for this lost genius, then thinks better of it.
"I made my way back home and discovered that I didn't have the key to the front gate -- I'd mixed it up with the key to the letter box. Which was useless."
"I need you to sign this document right here." He waves the paper and pen in front of the man's face. "It's important."
"I rang my neighbours' buzzers. It was late, and most of them didn't even answer. Those who did assumed I was trying to sell them something and hung up before I could even explain the situation..."
"I should definitely start thinking about jogging again."
"I think you said that *you* were the event, and that you would smash the looms of reality. Yeah... I knew I'd heard that looms line before."
"I used the profits from my agency to finance what I called a 'cultural incubator' -- abstract value generation, value per person, high-concept stuff..."
"I used to be a moderately-high-net-worth individual myself, if I can say so. I've *managed* big money before, played the game, hustled the movers of the marketing world..."
"I used to own my reality situation. My business buddies and I had our own creative services agency. I had a nice apartment, an even nicer piece of ass, but somehow it all got away from me..."

"I was a once a reasonably high-net-worth individual. A founder slash junior partner at a high-concept creative services agency. When my story begins, I had just landed a major contract with an insurance firm..."
"I was financing a group of poets in East Revachol who were developing a new, universal poetic language... but then it all went to shit..." He looks toward the bay.
"I was halfway done with my usual lap when it started to rain. The reality situation became very wet, very quickly."
"I wish I were, Tequila. I wish I were." He turns his head towards the skies. "Instead of my apartment key, I'd taken the key to the office."
"I'd rather not get into the details. It was pretty low-concept."
"I'll be damned... uh, well, uh... that's what we have Rosemary for!" He points to the third drunkard. "You can help, right?"
"I'm all ears, Tequila."
"I'm not even sure I should be telling you this story, to be perfectly honest. You're in a fragile state, and it might be too much for you to handle."
"I'm not sure. I think *you* were the event. Tequila Sunset. You know, as opposed to a Tequila Sunrise, which is *long gone*."
"I'm not surprised. Many men find it hard reaching that final level of genius without blow."
"I'm not taking a disgusting pile of hobo rags. I may be in an irrecoverably decaying orbit, but I've still got standards..."
"I'm pretty sure they all just want to snort it, though."

"I've never heard it mentioned outside of here... At first I thought it was a joke, to be honest. But I've been on the coast eight, nine months now and in that time I've seen at least three expeditions come through, searching for something."
"If I hadn't lost my keys that one time, I'd agree with you. But... life is a cruel mistress..." He takes a sip.
"If I knew where I lost it don't you think I'd have it? Come on, man!"
"If I knew where I lost it don't you think I'd have it? I mean -- maybe I was up by the boardwalk? Or walking along the beach? Or checking out the abandoned fish market?"
"If you find any, I'd be extremely grateful."
"In retrospect, I guess you lost your motor carriage, too. That's a big one."
"In that case, I'm not a storyteller." He crosses his legs and turns his gaze towards the ground.
"Interesting." He grabs the thermal cup and shakes it. "Ah, this is what they use to keep the working man going."
"Isn't it? All the pieces fit together perfectly. That's how I know it's right..."
"It definitely is."
"It depends, really. Are you willing to help me out?"
"It did. With my trusty Sansarique tracksuit I felt like I could conquer the world..."
"It helped, truly. With my trusty Sansarique Lickra(TM) tracksuit I felt like I could conquer the world..."
"It isn't? I thought that's what you were all about." He drags a hand down his face. "This is *fucking me up*, Tequila. I thought you'd love it -- honestly."
"It seemed pretty painful, to be honest with you. If I had to guess, I'd say you're still working through some shit."
"It was a day not unlike this one here..." You both glance skyward.

"It was a late Saturday night, when we, the Union of Moribund Alcoholics, were getting our drink on. Nothing remarkable about this, we get our drink on 24/7. Makes everything warm and glowy, I trust you know the feeling."
"It was the greatest thing this fishing village has seen since Rosemary tried to use a crab to open his beer."
"It's a big world out there, Tequila. Lotta lost jackets in it. Don't know why you'd think this could possibly be mine..."
"It's a hard thing for a man to confront his past." He nods. "That's why I avoid mine at all costs."
"It's a jungle out there... and in here."
"It's good to hear that you're on top of things. Talking about used to -- did you know that I *used* to be a real mover and shaker?" He thoughtfully picks at his shit-stained Lickra(TM) jacket.

"It's just not feasible within the economic and temporal frame of our current setup. Matter of fact, unless a bunch of money just falls out of the sky, we might *never* know what's up with that skull."
"It's the *Headless FALN Rider*. A headless man wearing a FALN tracksuit. Riding a horse. In search for the FALN cap that went missing -- when he lost his head."
"It's you. You're Tequila Sunset."
"Just head on over to the horseback monument. You'll see. World's gonna *know* -- about you, me, and the shiny numbers in our bank account."
"Just then I experienced a moment of clarity: I still had the key to my office! I could wait out the storm there..."
"Let me see. What? This isn't my jacket. My jacket was beautiful. This is fucking filthy! What am I supposed to do with this?"
"Let me see..." He takes the bottle and inspects it closely. "Ah, very high concept, thanks."
"Let your Personal Brand Strategist handle the timing, alright? You just focus on telling me what you liked about my work up there."
"Let's just move on. Anything else you want from me?"
"Listen, I can feel it in my guts -- a bright future awaits you, the one and only *Tequila Sunset*! You're already building great brand equity. No doubt the profits will come rolling in shortly."
"Listen, I know it might look a little *lacking* right now, but you gotta trust the process. I've got it all under control. Once the strike is over, the workers will be all over the monument..."
"Listen, I'm not about to come between you two. I know my place, eh? I'll just be your Personal Brand Strategist man. Your high-concept idea generator. Yeah?"
"Magic animals? No man, this is *serious stuff*..."
"Man, I thought you said you were a cool cop."
"Man, that's some grisly detail. Oh well, here's to another case closed!" He takes a hearty swig from his bottle.
"Man, you're like, bleeding now. Reality's really messed you up."
"Maybe you're right, who knows? Maybe we were behind the curve? We were fucking *rich*, though, that much I know..."
"Maybe you've heard? I used to be a very successful businessman. I've signed more than a few lease forms or whatever the fuck they were." He looks around. "Anyone got a pen? The pro's gonna do it."
"Maybe?" He takes a sip from his beer. "You look like you want to know how Tequila Sunset came to be. You look like you want to hear *the tale*."

"Me neither, Tequila. When I lost my keys, I lost more than access to my apartment -- I also lost my leverage over humanity. I wasn't a high-concept creative director anymore, I was just some homeless asshole with a premium Sansarique Lickra(TM) tracksuit."
"Mhm. Let me take a sip to moisten up my cords..." He takes a big sip, then begins: "Tequila Sunset rolled into Martinaise last Friday. And by *Tequila Sunset* I mean *you* -- the man, the myth."
"Mostly you kept shouting 'I am The Law' and talking about how you were going to bring the law to all lawless places with your law jaw."
"My agency, man..." He takes a long, melancholic sip. "The Boom Boom Room. Our concept was combining high art with the lowest forms of marketing -- the colour red, breasts, and oil painting..."
"My fellow members of the Union of Moribund Alcoholics? They're exactly what they look like."
"My jacket?"
"Nah, that name sucks. You're Tequila Sunset. Just embrace it, brother."
"Nah, this isn't it. 'FALN'? That's medium-concept stuff. Totally not my style."
"Naturally, loud noises pique the interest of anybody owning a pair of ears. That's just the reality we're in."
"Naturally, the situation required me to climb over the gate, which I did. There was no climbing down, because I slipped and landed on my ass."
"No can do. Sorry." He stares at the bottle in his hand, then lets out a deep sigh...
"No fucking way. Idiot Doom Spiral never forgets a piece of premium menswear..."

"No need to worry about *that*," he says, his inebriated mouth twisting into odd shapes, "I've got it *all* under control. Besides, it helps with my creativity. Gets the business juices flowing, y'know?" He finishes it off with a wink.
"No one does it better than me, eh?" He claps his hands in delight. "I was able to get it all together -- and *so fast* too. No wonder I used to be an industry leader..."
